meta.title_tag: Dog Breed Cost Index 2026: 164 Breeds Compared
meta.quick_answer: Across the 164 breeds in Wooffy's cost guides, a puppy from a reputable breeder typically costs $1,200–$2,500 (median range), the first year of ownership runs $3,265–$6,535, and each year after that about $1,490–$2,700. Size is the biggest driver: giant breeds cost roughly 1.8× as much in year one as toy breeds. The most expensive first year is the Leonberger ($6,000–$12,000); the least expensive is the Russell Terrier ($1,800–$3,500).
meta.author: Kailun Zhang

hero.alt: Dog breed cost index: first-year and annual ownership costs for 164 breeds, compared

intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: What does a dog cost in 2026?
intro.html:
This index puts the numbers from all 164 of our first-year cost guides side by side: what a puppy costs to buy, what the first year adds up to once vet visits, spay or neuter, food, insurance, grooming and setup are counted, and what a typical year costs after that. Every figure is a low–high range in US dollars for a dog bought from a reputable, health-testing breeder; rescue adoption is usually far cheaper up front (see each breed's guide for its rescue range).

Use the first-year cost calculator to adjust these ranges for your own region, food choice and insurance plan. Figures last compiled 2026-10-15.

highlights.label: Highlights
highlights.heading: Which dog breeds cost the most and least to own?
highlights.html:
Most expensive first year

  1. Leonberger — $6,000–$12,000
  2. Dogue de Bordeaux — $6,340–$11,250
  3. Afghan Hound — $5,592–$11,746
  4. Belgian Malinois — $5,300–$11,800
  5. Tibetan Mastiff — $5,159–$11,780
  6. Samoyed — $5,550–$11,000
  7. Neapolitan Mastiff — $5,500–$11,000
  8. Bloodhound — $5,550–$10,600
  9. Cane Corso — $4,450–$11,500
  10. Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier — $5,160–$10,670

Least expensive first year

  1. Russell Terrier — $1,800–$3,500
  2. Chihuahua — $1,680–$4,200
  3. Australian Terrier — $2,000–$4,000
  4. Parson Russell Terrier — $2,000–$4,000
  5. Border Terrier — $2,100–$4,100
  6. Harrier — $2,250–$4,050
  7. Bluetick Coonhound — $2,300–$4,200
  8. American Water Spaniel — $2,300–$4,450
  9. Schipperke — $2,326–$4,495
  10. Basset Hound — $2,500–$4,500

Highest and lowest puppy prices

Highest: Afghan Hound ($3,500–$7,000), Bloodhound ($3,500–$7,000), Samoyed ($3,200–$6,500), Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier ($3,000–$6,500), Irish Setter ($3,000–$6,000). Lowest: Beagle ($500–$1,200), Black and Tan Coonhound ($600–$1,200), Bluetick Coonhound ($600–$1,200), Dalmatian ($600–$1,200), American Foxhound ($500–$1,500).

methodology.label: Methodology
methodology.heading: Where do these numbers come from?
methodology.html:
The figures come from Wooffy's 164 breed-specific first-year cost guides, each researched and written for that breed. In July 2026 we extracted every guide's line items into one structured dataset and checked that each first-year total matched the sum of its parts; 22 totals that did not were corrected in October 2026. The index is regenerated from that dataset whenever a guide is updated.

What the columns mean: Puppy price is the typical range from a reputable breeder who runs the breed's recommended health tests. First year adds the first-year vet schedule, spay or neuter, food, insurance, grooming and one-time setup (crate, bed, bowls, leash). Each year after is food, routine vet care, insurance and grooming for an adult dog. Emergencies, training classes, boarding and dog walkers are excluded. Where a guide gave no explicit figure for a line (for example spay or neuter), a regional estimate is used; this affects 81 breeds and is noted on each guide.

You are welcome to cite or reproduce these figures with a link to this page. For a per-breed estimate adjusted to your situation, use the first-year cost calculator.

faq.q: How much does a dog cost in the first year?
faq.a: Across 164 breeds, the median first-year range is $3,265–$6,535, including the puppy, vet care, spay or neuter, food, insurance, grooming and setup. Toy breeds median $2,550–$5,450; giant breeds median $4,575–$9,465.

faq.q: What is the cheapest dog breed to own?
faq.a: By first-year cost, the least expensive breeds in this index are the Russell Terrier ($1,800–$3,500), Chihuahua ($1,680–$4,200) and Australian Terrier ($2,000–$4,000). Small, short-coated breeds with modest grooming needs sit at the bottom of the index.

faq.q: What is the most expensive dog breed to own?
faq.a: The Leonberger has the highest first-year range in this index at $6,000–$12,000, followed by the Dogue de Bordeaux ($6,340–$11,250) and Afghan Hound ($5,592–$11,746). Giant size, high puppy prices and professional grooming drive the top of the list.

faq.q: How much does a dog cost per year after the first year?
faq.a: The median ongoing range is $1,490–$2,700 a year for food, routine vet care, insurance and grooming. It scales with size: roughly $1,235–$2,200 for toy breeds and $2,200–$4,200 for giant breeds.

faq.q: Where do these numbers come from?
faq.a: From Wooffy's own 164 first-year cost guides, extracted into one dataset in July 2026 and cross-checked so every total equals its line items. Ranges are US dollars for a puppy from a reputable breeder; emergencies and optional services are excluded.
